// Command corpus is the conformance suite's tool under test.
//
// Deliberately awkward. Each operation exists because it is a shape a surface
// could plausibly get wrong on its own: nested objects, arrays whose values
// contain commas, integers past the float64 boundary, text that is not ASCII,
// binary that is not text at all, and a handler that fails.
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/richardwooding/forge/sdk/tool"
)

type EchoArgs struct {
	Text string `json:"text" jsonschema:"text to echo back"`
}

type NestArgs struct {
	Outer struct {
		Inner struct {
			Value string `json:"value"`
		} `json:"inner"`
	} `json:"outer"`
	Count int `json:"count,omitempty"`
}

type NestOut struct {
	Value string `json:"value"`
	Count int    `json:"count"`
}

type TagArgs struct {
	Tags []string `json:"tags,omitempty" jsonschema:"tags, which may contain commas"`
}

type TagOut struct {
	Joined string `json:"joined"`
	N      int    `json:"n"`
}

type BigArgs struct {
	N int64 `json:"n" jsonschema:"an integer that must survive exactly"`
}

type BigOut struct {
	N int64 `json:"n"`
}

type ModeArgs struct {
	Mode string `json:"mode" jsonschema:"one of fast or slow"`
}

var _ = tool.Register(
	tool.Spec{
		Name:    "corpus",
		Version: "1.0.0",
		Summary: "Shapes that surfaces get wrong",
		Labels:  []string{"conformance", "demo"},
	},
	tool.Op("echo", echo, tool.Text(), tool.ReadOnly(),
		tool.Summary("Return the text unchanged")),
	tool.Op("nest", nest, tool.ReadOnly(),
		tool.Summary("Read a value from three levels down")),
	tool.Op("tags", tags, tool.ReadOnly(),
		tool.Summary("Join a list whose values contain commas")),
	tool.Op("big", big, tool.ReadOnly(),
		tool.Summary("Round-trip an integer past 2^53")),
	tool.Op("mode", mode, tool.Text(), tool.ReadOnly(),
		tool.Summary("Accept only one of two values")),
	tool.Op("blob", blob, tool.Bytes("application/octet-stream"),
		tool.Summary("Return bytes that are not text")),
	tool.Op("fail", fail, tool.Text(),
		tool.Summary("Always fail, with a message worth keeping")),
	tool.Op("panics", panics, tool.Text(),
		tool.Summary("Always panic")),
)

func main() {}

func echo(ctx *tool.Context, a EchoArgs) (string, error) { return a.Text, nil }

func nest(ctx *tool.Context, a NestArgs) (NestOut, error) {
	return NestOut{Value: a.Outer.Inner.Value, Count: a.Count}, nil
}

func tags(ctx *tool.Context, a TagArgs) (TagOut, error) {
	return TagOut{Joined: strings.Join(a.Tags, "|"), N: len(a.Tags)}, nil
}

func big(ctx *tool.Context, a BigArgs) (BigOut, error) { return BigOut{N: a.N}, nil }

func mode(ctx *tool.Context, a ModeArgs) (string, error) {
	if a.Mode != "fast" && a.Mode != "slow" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("mode %q is neither fast nor slow", a.Mode)
	}
	return "mode:" + a.Mode, nil
}

func blob(ctx *tool.Context, a EchoArgs) ([]byte, error) {
	// A zero byte and a byte that is not valid UTF-8, so a surface that treats
	// binary as text is caught rather than flattered.
	return []byte{0x00, 0xff, 0x10, 'o', 'k'}, nil
}

func fail(ctx *tool.Context, a EchoArgs) (string, error) {
	return "", errors.New("corpus: deliberate failure: " + a.Text)
}

func panics(ctx *tool.Context, a EchoArgs) (string, error) {
	panic("corpus: deliberate panic: " + a.Text)
}
